description: Each token is a single centered emblem on a near-black charcoal ground: one dominant primitive — a hexagon, a circle, or occasionally a rotated square/diamond — filled with a translucent desaturated slate blue-grey, with two or three smaller versions of the same or a related shape nested concentrically inside it, and a scatter of small satellite shapes (hexagons, squares, dots) either orbiting the perimeter at roughly radial stations or clustered onto the body. The palette is severely restricted to three notes: charcoal void, slate blue-grey mass, and a muted brass/ochre gold used only as a minority accent — a thin outline, an annulus rim, a satellite fill, or a single centre dot. Everything is semi-transparent, so overlaps read as tonal steps rather than as new colours, and the whole object floats with generous margin, occupying roughly half to two-thirds of the frame with no edge-to-edge composition; a few tokens (10264, 10622, 10801, 10980) fling one or two orphan gold satellites far out toward the frame corner, detached from the body and in one case nearly clipped. What the twelve share is centredness, three- or six-fold radial symmetry, nesting, and the same three-note palette; what separates them is the base primitive (hexagon / circle / diamond), the count and radius of the satellites (none at all, six evenly orbiting, three clustered lobes, or a dense chaotic corona), and where gold lands — rim, outline, speck, or satellite fill. Across the three conditions the object holds its identity and changes by contraction and ornament: stress shrinks the body, strips the gold almost entirely (9369 loses its whole gold rim, 9190's satellites shrink to grey stubs, 9548's corona vanishes) and flattens toward a single soft grey mass, while recovery inflates the form and floods the gold back in heavier than neutral (9011 gains a bold gold hexagonal outline it never had, 9369's rim becomes a thick saturated annulus, 9548 grows a denser corona than neutral, 9190 gains a heavy gold inner ring plus gold-filled satellites).
seenAt120: The silhouette survives cleanly — hexagon vs circle vs diamond is unambiguous, the orbiting satellites read as a bumped or spiky ring, and the gold survives as a rim, an outline, or a speck of colour, which is what carries most of the differentiation at this size. What is lost is the internal nesting: the translucent inner shapes collapse into a single flat grey blob in the plainer tokens, so 9011, 10622 and 10801 all reduce to 'grey hexagon with a faint interior and one gold speck' and are hard to tell apart, and 10264 and 10980 both reduce to 'cluster of grey hexagons with gold bits'. Roughly nine or ten of the twelve remain individually recognisable at browse size. The condition changes remain very legible at 120px, because they act on the two things that survive — overall bulk and how much gold is present.
